For those [other practices], if they produce an effect in this world, do harm in the next; whereas this which we set forth is of benefit both in this world and in the next. And God is the granter of success in what is right.
Chapter 1 (al-bāb al-awwal): On the letters of the alphabet (ḥurūf al- muʿjam) and the secrets and concealments (iḍmārāt) they contain

Faṣl. In it I speak first of the letters of the alphabet, since they are the roots of speech and its foundation, and by them its edifice is raised up. Know that numbers have secrets, just as letters have effects, and that the upper world supplies the lower world. For the world of the Throne supplies the world of the Footstool; the world of the Footstool supplies the sphere of Saturn; the sphere of Saturn supplies the sphere of Jupiter; the sphere of Jupiter supplies the sphere of Mars; the sphere of Mars supplies the sphere of the Sun; the sphere of the Sun supplies the sphere of Venus; the sphere of Venus supplies the sphere of Mercury; the sphere of Mercury supplies the sphere of the Moon; the sphere of the Moon supplies the sphere of heat; the sphere of heat supplies the sphere of air; the sphere of air supplies the sphere of water; and the sphere of water supplies the sphere of earth. To Saturn, among the celestial [letters], belongs the letter (jīm), and the numbers that fall to it are three in sum; but in detail, fifty-three, thus: the mīm as forty, the yāʾ as ten, and the jīm as three — and it is likewise [written] with three letters. To it, among the terrestrial [letters], belongs the letter (ṣād), which in number is ninety; and to it belongs the threefold square (al-muthallath). To the sphere of Jupiter belongs the letter (dāl), which is four in number, and to it belongs the fourfold square (al-murabbaʿ), which is four multiplied by four. The operative deployment of the sphere of Mars, among the celestial [letters], is five in sum; it is the letter (hāʾ), and of the awfāq it has the fivefold (al-mukhammas). To the sphere of the Sun belongs six; it is the letter (wāw), and of the awfāq it has the sixfold (al-musaddas). As for the operative deployment of the sphere of Venus, [it is] seven; it is the letter (zāy), and of the awfāq it has the sevenfold (al-musabbaʿ). As for the operative deployment of the sphere of Mercury, it has of number eight; it is the letter (ḥāʾ), and of the awfāq it has the eightfold (al-muthamman). As for the operative deployment of the sphere of the Moon, it has /fol. 4r./ of number nine; it is the letter (ṭāʾ), and of the awfāq it has the ninefold (al-mutassaʿ). And Saturn has the threefold square that is renowned among the learned. Understand, and you will be rightly guided.

Faṣl, on the relation of the human essence. The Throne has the letter (alif); the Footstool has the letter (bāʾ); Saturn has the letter (jīm); and so likewise on down to the Moon, according to what has been set out before it. Understand.

Faṣl. The letters are of [several] kinds. Some of them are begun from the right — these are the letters of the Arabs; and some of them are begun from the left — these are the Byzantine, the Greek, and the Coptic. Every script written toward the right is joined, and every script written toward the left is disjoined and not connected. Understand.

Faṣl. The letters are twenty-eight, apart from lām-alif, with which they come to a full twenty-nine; and that is the number of the lunar mansions. And since fourteen of the mansions appear above the earth, so likewise among these letters there are those that are assimilated to the lām of the definite article — fourteen letters, namely these:
; and there are those that appear distinctly with it, likewise fourteen letters, namely these: .

Faṣl. The first of the letters is the alif, and those letters that come after it — such as the ṭāʾs, the taʿrīfāt, and the rāʾs — are from the flanks of the alif. When one looks upon the letters, he finds that they leave an impress upon the soul, so that they come to exist in the soul before they exist in [outward] shape. The alif among the letters is the one among the numbers, and numbers possess a spiritual and subtle power. Numbers are among the secrets of words, just as letters are among the secrets of acts. Numbers have, in the human world, secrets and benefits which the

Maker — exalted be His power — has set in order, just as He set in order within the letters the secrets of benefit, such as invocation and incantations (ruqā) and other things whose effect has appeared in the sensible world through the various kinds of names. And know that no time confines the letters; rather they act by [their] occult property for whoever wishes [to employ them], whereas the numbers act by the natures, and so they are bound up with the celestial elections (ikhtiyārāt).

The letter (dāl) has of numbers four. So whoever sets up a figure of four multiplied by four and places within it a numerical proportion — and that on the day of Monday, the day of the Prophet's birth, God bless him and grant him peace, the day of his mission, and the day of his death — and let that be while the Moon is in its exaltation at three degrees of Taurus, free of the malefics, and while the hour is the Moon's: you write it after the purity of ablution and a prayer of two rakʿas with the Throne Verse and And say: He is God, One (Q 112:1) one hundred times, upon clean parchment. Whoever carries this written wafq with him, God — exalted is He — will make easy for him memorization, understanding, and wisdom, and his worth will be magnified in the eyes of the upper world and the lower world entire. And if a prisoner hangs it upon himself, he goes forth from his prison forthwith /fol. 4v./. And if this parchment is carried upon a banner, the enemies among the unbelievers and the rebellious are routed by it. And whoever carries it with him and disputes while holding it overcomes his adversary — because this letter, which is the dāl, has as the numbers that fall to it four, and its figure is four multiplied by four. And dirya(?) — Jupiter has special claim to it, and it is a benefic planet. The dāl is, in sum, a cold letter; and by it God completed the four natures — fire, air, water, and earth — which are yellow bile, blood, phlegm, and black bile. These, then, are four for four; and so it possesses the power of the natures and their equilibrium. This noble letter appears in His name al-Dāʾim (the Everlasting) in particular, and in His name al-Wadūd (the Loving) in general, since affection (wudd) is shared while everlastingness stands alone. For that reason the wāw comes before [the dāl] in al-Wadūd, whereas in al-Dāʾim nothing comes before the dāl.

And for that reason it occurs in the two noble and mighty names, Aḥmad and Muḥammad — God bless him and grant him peace — and that at the end of the two noble and generous names; because it points to everlastingness and to the last of the ultimate end: there is no god but He. So it is, after the dāl, for everlastingness. It comes first in His name al-Dāʾim only because to Him belongs perpetuity, first and last; and so He gave His servants a share in the perpetuity of subsistence in the hereafter, after annihilation. This letter is one of the letters of the Throne, because the Throne's existence does not alter, since it is the first of the world of originations and the first of the world of everlasting duration. To it are the ascents of the spirits; in it are the ranks of the intellects; and in it are the lights of Mercy. Most of the gnostics of God — exalted is He — have had this unveiled to them, according to the portion apportioned to them. Among them is Ḥāritha — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — when the Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, questioned him and said to him: ((How have you risen this morning, O Ḥāritha? Ḥāritha said: O Messenger of God, I have risen a true believer. The Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: Every truth has a reality; what is the reality of your faith? He said: I have risen having turned my soul away from this world, so that its stone and its gold are alike in my sight, and its living and its dead, and its rich and its poor; and it is as though I were looking upon the Throne of the All-Merciful brought forth into view, and upon the people being driven to the Reckoning — to the Garden and to the Fire. The Messenger of God, God bless him and grant him peace, said to him: You have known; now hold fast.)) And the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said concerning the spirits: ((When they pass the night in the purity of ablution, they spend the night prostrate beneath the Throne.))

The letter dāl has among its secrets perpetuity and subsistence; and al-Dāʾim is a name among the names of God, exalted is He, [the name of] pre-eternity and post-eternity, and none but God, exalted is He, is named by it. As for al-Wadūd, affection is shared, as has preceded — and that is because affection (wudd) is the outward of love (ḥubb), and love is the inward of affection; so the first of affection is love (maḥabba). Affection divides into two divisions, an outward and an inward: its outward is affection and its inward is love. The dwelling place of affection is the heart, and it is the most disclosive of the worlds of the heart. Passionate love (ʿishq) is a subtlety between love and affection; its dwelling place is the pericardium (shaghaf). And love is the inward of passionate love, and its dwelling place is /fol. 5r./ the inmost heart (fuʾād) — for the heart has three cavities. The first of them is in its upper part, in that which is dense of it; it is a light that blazes up, and it is the locus of islām, and the meanings of the letters there are obscure. It is also the seat of the rational faculty in man and of the faculty that governs the meanings of the volition arising from the soul. The second is in the middle of the heart; it is the seat of reflection and recollection, and it is a shining light, and it is the seat of the indwelling peace (sakīna), and it is the seat of imagination with respect to what the spirit casts into it. The third is at its far end; it is the thinnest and subtlest of them, and it is denoted by the term fuʾād. It is the seat of faith, of the intellect, of light, of operative disposal, and of the secrets; [it is] the balance of the intellect and the subtleties of the wisdoms. It is the seat of love, and the seat of natural life deriving from the subtle heat.

This fuʾād has a luminous eye by which it apprehends the realities of the things of the Dominion (malakūt) and the secrets of the celestial things of the Omnipotence (jabarūt), and the balances of the realities. It is the seat of the lights of divine bestowal and of the secrets of the celestial things; and that is the inner sight (baṣīra) by which one sees. He said: For truly it is not the eyes that go blind, but rather it is the hearts within the breasts that go blind (Q 22:46). And the middle cavity — it is the seat of passionate love, and it is a luminous eye by which seeking is apprehended, and from it there arises earnestness in seeking and yearning for the thing sought; and it is the quickest to attach itself to persons.

— on account of its subtlety. By it the world of sovereign rule (ʿālam al-mulk) and all that it contains of the handiwork of God — exalted is He — is unveiled, and by it there comes about the finding of beauty in things beautiful. Then, to the first cavity there belongs a luminous eye by which it looks upon the secrets of sensible things, the phases of composite things, the realities of the letters and their secrets, and the immensity of what God — exalted is He — has deposited in them of the secrets of the names and the realities of the gnoses they impart. By it came its affection (wudd) for the servants of God, and its magnifying of God — exalted is He — on account of its knowledge, by reason of what God — exalted is He — has graciously bestowed upon it in its unveiling of the secrets of sensible things. These are the inner sights (baṣāʾir) of the hearts, all of them; save that men are disparate in the divergence of their states. We have already set forth in Mawāqīt al-baṣāʾir wa-laṭāʾif al-sarāʾir ("The Appointed Times of the Inner Sights and the Subtleties of the Innermost Secrets") that the spirits of revelation in the Book of God — exalted is He — are three: the Trustworthy Spirit (al-rūḥal-amīn), the Holy Spirit (rūḥal-qudus), and the Spirit of the Command (rūḥal-amr). The revelation from the Trustworthy Spirit descended upon the first cavity, because it is the isthmus (barzakh) that lies between speech and the tongue; and so it is the first of the degrees of revelation in the sending-down, each receiving according to what God has apportioned to him of God's inspiration upon the hearts. After it comes the Holy Spirit, and it pours forth the lights of what is set down in the Preserved Tablet upon the second degree of the heart, so that faith and intellective insight are made firm, and the kinds of wisdom, the kinds of Lordly supplies, and the subtleties of faith appear. Then the third degree, which is the locus of the most holy light; and it is likewise the locus of hearing, and it is the locus of the intellect. God — exalted is He — said to His prophet Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace, in His Mighty Book: For you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call (Q 30:52). By that He did not intend the death of sense-perception; He intended by it only the death of unbelief and disobedience. /fol. 5v./ Nor did He intend by "the deaf" a deafness of the ears, for the faculty of hearing is present; He intended by it only this hearing which is in the world of the inmost heart (fuʾād), and that is the locus of the intellect and the locus of the descent of the Spirit of the Command, which points to empowerment (tamkīn) and to the reality of union (jamʿ); and none was singled out for this sending-down save Muḥammad, God bless him and grant him peace. We have expounded the valleys of the hearts, their treasuries, their lights, and their inner sights in our book known as Mawāqif al-ghāyāt fī asrār al-riyāḍāt ("The Stations of the Ultimate Ends, on the Secrets of the Spiritual Disciplines"); ponder it there and you will find it soundly set out, if God — exalted is He — wills. God — exalted is He — said: Those who believe and do righteous deeds — the All-Merciful will appoint for them affection (Q 19:96): that is, He brings into being in their hearts an affection by which they show affection to Him. This is because they instil affection into their hearts by the varieties of the litanies of remembrance (adhkār) and the modes of the acts of drawing near, so that they leave nothing of the works of the heart which they do not put to operative use; and they instil affection into their souls only by severing habits and familiar attachments, until there accrues to them an affection from God — exalted is He — so that their speech turns into the utterance of wisdom and their movements into an ascent of degrees. And he instils affection into his spirit by the realities of faith, the secrets of the revealed Law, and the lights of religion, until the traces of affection appear upon the spirit; then he beholds the Return by unveiling, and what God — exalted is He — has prepared therein of the kinds of bliss for His friends and of chastisement for His enemies, so that its flame increases in the seeking of the return to God, glorified and exalted, and in the longing for the meeting with God — exalted is He. And he instils affection into his intellect by reflecting upon the things God — exalted is He — has fashioned, and upon what God, blessed and exalted, has deposited in them of the secrets of His signs; and he instils affection into it by abandoning all entanglements and familiar attachments; and he instils affection into it by complying with His command, since it rests upon the root of purity, and commands only good and knows only good. And when the heart turns toward affection, it comes to gaze upon the secrets of the wonders of the Dominion (malakūt), upon the modes of the revelatory and inspirational addresses, and upon the celestial realities. We have gone on at length.

Let us now return to what we were about, concerning the letter dāl and its benefits. It is this: whoever writes the letter dāl thirty-five times — that being the number which falls to it when it is spelled out in detail, for when you write dāl in full the lām is thirty, the dāl is four, and the alif is one, so that the total is thirty-five — together with its square figure, upon a white silk cloth, and encircles it with the letter dāl thirty-five times, the Moon being in the house of Cancer and safeguarded from Jupiter, and sets it inside the bezel of a ring at that time, and wears it in a state of ritual purity, of fasting, and of inward clarity: God — exalted is He — will perpetuate for him the favour in which he stands, and will establish him in every outward undertaking, and God will make his provision ample. And whoever multiplies the remembrance of His name al-Dāʾim (the Everlasting) shall have that. We have mentioned this and expounded it in sum, under the name al-Dāʾim and the dāl of al-ḥamd (praise), in our book ʿIlm al-hudā wa-asrār al-ihtidāʾ ("The Science of Right Guidance and the Secrets of Being Guided"), under His name al-Raḥmān; so I need not repeat it.

And whoever draws it in this form, as its explanation will follow, and carries it with him, will attain all his aims and what he seeks from kings and rulers; women will love him and he will obtain from them an abundant share; and no woman will look upon him but she will love him, by the leave of God — exalted is He. And this is its form: /fol. 6r./

Some of them have mentioned that whoever writes "Muḥammad is the Messenger of God, Aḥmad is the Messenger of God" thirty-five times after the Friday prayer and carries it with him, God — exalted is He —

will grant him strength for obedience and aid unto blessing, and will suffice him against the promptings of the satans. And if he keeps up his gazing upon that slip (biṭāqa) while calling to mind the name of the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — Muḥammad, and his name Aḥmad, and how these two noble names, magnified, venerated, and blessed, were completed by this noble letter, namely the dāl, and if he persists in gazing upon them both every day at sunrise while invoking blessings upon the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — our master Muḥammad, God will make easy for him on that day of his the means of felicity. That is in proportion to [his] receptivity, to the resolve of intention, and to inward clarity; and this is a very subtle secret. And whoever writes the numerical square figure and carries it, God — exalted is He — will keep him safe from harmful enemies, from whichever of the worlds they may be. And whoever writes it, washes it off, and gives it to drink to one afflicted with an unremitting fever, that will benefit him; likewise it alleviates the pain of the venom for one stung by scorpions or bitten by serpents, and other such matters as befit this chapter. And this is the form of the square that has been mentioned:
/fol. 6v./
[Figure [2 .

As for its literal square figure, its occult property is that it takes away forgetfulness and sharpens the understanding and the intellect, for whoever persists in drinking it in rainwater and bees' honey. It also benefits one who suffers in his chest. And if it is engraved — with the Moon in Scorpio and Mars looking upon it with a look of enmity — upon a plate of copper which you heat in the fire, it is efficacious for the scorpion's sting, if its water is given to drink after the ring has been dipped in it.

Now since this square figure is the sum of the four alifs, which are the secret of the intellect, the secret of the spirit, the secret of the soul, and the secret of the heart — for the alif in number is one, and when you multiply the four by itself it spreads out to sixteen — that is the limit of the number taken in detail, because the Throne, the Footstool, the seven heavens and the seven earths: the total is sixteen. And this number is the limit of this square figure, which is sixteen cells. So within this sixteen there is the evenness (shafʿiyya) of fourteen, namely the seven heavens and the seven earths. And within it there is the evenness of twelve, namely the twelve zodiacal signs. And within it there is the evenness of eight, which is the evenness of the Bearers of the Throne. And within it there is the evenness of six, which is the evenness of the bodily bounds, namely: above, below, behind, in front, right, and left. And within it there is the evenness of four, which is the evenness of the prophets, the truthful ones, the martyrs, and the righteous. And within it there is the evenness of two, namely the testimony that there is no god but God and that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God. These, then, are seven evens. And within it there is, of the odd, the odd number (watr) fifteen, which is the Footstool, the seven heavens and the seven earths. And within it there is the odd number thirteen, which is the oddness of the Pen, the Tablet, the Trumpet, the Holy Spirit, the Footstool, and the seven heavens. And within it there is the oddness of eleven, which is what is in the world of man: the five senses — namely hearing, sight, smell, taste, and touch — and the six directions: above, below, right, left, behind, and in front. And within it there is the odd number nine, which is the essence of man and his eight natures, namely heat and dryness and cold and moisture, and heat and moisture and cold and dryness, and heat and dryness and cold and moisture; for yellow bile is hot and dry, and air is hot and moist — that being the nature of blood — and phlegm's nature is cold and moist, and black bile is cold and dry: these are eight, taken separately. And within it /fol. 7r./ there is the odd number seven, which is the odd number of the seven spheres: the sphere of Saturn, the sphere of Jupiter, the sphere of Mars, the sphere of the Sun, the sphere of Venus, the sphere of Mercury, and the sphere of the Moon; and it is the odd number of the seven days and of the seven earths and of everything sevenfold. And within it there is the odd number five, which is the odd number of the five prayers. And within it there is the odd number three, which is the odd number of the three abodes: the abode of this world, the abode of the barzakh, and the abode of the hereafter. And within it there is the odd number one, which is the intellect. Thus there are gathered in the sixteen seven evens and eight odds; and every even meets every odd, and every odd meets every even. An example of that: one and one are two, and three and three are six, and so on to the end of them; and likewise with the evens. And this is its numerical figure in the natural script, which is the Indian, in this form; and this script is the more fitting and the more proper for it.

And it has, in the letters, wondrous secrets — namely, that you set letters in the place of these numbers. Your working with them shall be after a fast of two weeks, in which by night you eat nothing but bread alone, together with the maintaining of ritual purity and the remembrance of God — exalted is He. Then you betake yourself to a square plate of refined tin and engrave upon it this literal figure, facing the qibla, after praying two rakʿas with the Throne Verse and Say: He is God, One (Q 112:1) a hundred times, on Thursday, in the hour of Jupiter, at sunrise, with the Moon safeguarded from Jupiter and from the Sun, and with the ascendant being Gemini; and you suffumigate it with mastic and white sandalwood every Thursday. Then the wearer of this ring — God, exalted is He, will make the affairs of religious observance beloved to him, and will make easy for him works and acts of obedience, and he will be granted ease

…in the means of livelihood, and God, exalted is He, will place blessing in whatever he undertakes with his hand. Likewise, if he sets it in his place of business, or in his shop, or in his strongbox, his wealth will grow great and his provision abundant — on condition that he write together with it the wording proper to the request for provision, for ample expansion, and for the placing of blessing, according to what comes hereafter, if God, exalted is He, wills.

Whoever writes it upon gazelle parchment on a Thursday at sunrise, and carries it with him sewn into his garments, will be kept safe, by the power of God, exalted is He, from thieves and from every hateful thing, and from all that he fears and is wary of — after he has written together with it the wording befitting it for all of that. And beware of carrying it in a state of ritual impurity. This is the first of the arrangements of the numbers. I shall inform you of something of the secrets of the numbers, and of what God, exalted is He, has brought forth within them, and of the description of their benefits and their operative deployments; and of the secret of the letters of the alphabet (al-ḥurūf al-muʿjama) that are in the Book of God, exalted is He — that is, the openings of the suras, which are twenty-eight suras — upon which none look save the elect among His creatures; and of what is contained in the Most Beautiful Names of God, exalted is He, which are the treasuries of the secrets /fol. 7v./ and the channels of the decrees; and of the knowledge of the Greatest Name of God, exalted is He, the Mighty, the Great, the Greater, the Generous, the Most Generous, and of what it contains of the divine secrets and the attributes of Lordship — such as you will not find in any book, nor light upon in any register, from what I have gathered and inscribed of the pearls of the sciences and the recondite secrets, so that whoever reads it and understands its meaning may profit by it.

This is the form of the letter-square (al-murabbaʿ al-ḥarfī), as you see. It has an invocation composed from its figure, assembled from its letters, which are these:(alif),(bāʾ),(jīm),(dāl),(hāʾ), (wāw), (zāy), (ḥāʾ),(ṭāʾ),(yāʾ) — the letter yāʾ having been added to them, it being the tenth.
[Wafq: 4×4, letter form — cells as in source; abjad values in parentheses] [Fig. 3]

And out of them the noble invocation is ordered. You say: "O God, I ask You by all Your Most Beautiful Names, those of them that I know and those that I do not know. Yā Hū, Yā Hū, Yā Wāḥid (O One), Yā Aḥad (O Unique), Yā Hādī (O Guide), Yā Barr (O Beneficent), Yā Bāriʾ (O Fashioner), Yā Baṣīr (O All-Seeing), Yā Badīʿ (O Wondrous Originator), Yā Bāsiṭ (O Expander), Yā Bāqī (O Abiding), Yā Jalīl (O Majestic), Yā Dāʾim (O Everlasting), Yā Wārith (O Inheritor), Yā Wadūd (O Loving), Yā Ḥayy (O Living), Yā Ḥalīm (O Forbearing), Yā Ḥaqq (O Truth), Yā
Ḥakīm (O Wise), Yā Ẓāhir (O Manifest), Yā Muẓhir (O Revealer). Fulfil my need! Answer, O Isrāfīl, you and your helpers and your servant-spirits from among the dwellers of the heavens and the earth!"

Now since it has already been set forth that the letters are twenty-eight, according to the number of the twenty-eight lunar mansions, that part of them which is visible above the earth is fourteen mansions, and beneath the earth fourteen mansions; so that when one mansion sets, the fifteenth, which is its counterpart, rises — thus for ever. For that reason fifteen of the letters are dotted and thirteen are undotted. The dotted ones are these:

. The undotted ones are these: .Those of them that are undotted are the mansions of the auspicious influences, and those of them that are dotted are the mansions of the inauspicious influences and of the mixed. Whichever of them has a single dot is nearer to the auspicious; whichever of them has two dots is intermediate among the inauspicious, and it is the mixed; and whichever of them has three dots is at the utmost — it is a greater malefic, as for example shīn ()and thāʾ (.)Ponder that. Here now I make plain to you the manner of it. It is this: that the mansions are figures of differing disposition within the divine creation, no one of them resembling another; whereas the moon — /fol. 8r./ God, exalted is He, created it round, and likewise the sun, for a hidden secret that cannot be expounded, because to divulge the secret of Lordship is unbelief. As for the moon, when it descends into the mansion of al-Naṭḥ, there are indications that point to it, and words [to be spoken]; but walls have ears, and concealment is the better course. So understand what we have indicated and ponder it. And God, exalted is He, speaks the truth, and He guides to the way.
The Elements of the Letters
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 15

The twenty-eight letters that exist are divided among the ʿanāṣir-i arbaʿa (the four elements), with seven (7) letters belonging to each element. These letters and the elements to which they belong are as follows:
[I 16] 1. The element of Fire: The letters belonging to this element are maftūḥ (open). They are dry and hot, of a choleric (ṣafrāwī) nature.
The direction of the fire letters is east; they are attracting and dominant.
The letters belonging to Fire are these:
Dhāl, Shin, Fe, Mīm, Ṭāʾ, He, Alif 2. The element of Earth: The letters belonging to this element are majzūm (cut off). They are dry and cold, of a melancholic (sawdāwī)
nature. The direction of the earth letters is south; they are attracted rather than attracting, and dominated.
The letters belonging to Earth are these:
Ḍād, Te, Sat, Nun, Ye, Wāw, Be 3. The element of Air: The letters belonging to this element are maghmūm (closed). They are moist and hot, of a sanguine (damawī)
nature. The direction of the air letters is west; they are attracting and dominant.
The letters belonging to Air are these:
Ẓāʾ, Se, Qāf, Sin, Kāf, Ze, Jīm 4. The element of Water: The letters belonging to this element are maksūr (broken). They are moist and cold, of a phlegmatic nature.
The direction of the water letters is north; they are attracted rather than attracting, and dominated.
The letters belonging to Water are these:
Ghayn, Khāʾ, Ra, ʿAyn, Lam, Ha, Dal
Luminous and Dark Letters
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 16
Of the twenty-eight (28) letters, fourteen (14) are set apart as nurani (luminous) and fourteen (14) as zulmani (dark).
[I 17] The luminous (nurani) letters are these:
Ye, He, Nun, Mīm, Lam, Kāf, Qāf, ʿAyn, Ṭāʾ, Sat, Sin, Ra, Ha, Alif The dark (zulmani) letters are these:
Wāw, Fe, ʿAyn, Ẓāʾ, Ḍād, Shin, Ze, Dhāl, Dal, Khāʾ, Jīm, Se, Te, Be
The Four Elements and Their Natures
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 17
The ʿAnāṣir Arbaʿa (Four Elements) are Fire, Earth, Air, and Water.
Each of these has its own nature.

The nature of Fire is dry and hot. The nature of Earth is dry and cold. The nature of Air is moist and hot. The nature of Water is moist and cold. Heat becomes mu'tedil (balanced, temperate) when joined with cold, and dryness when joined with moisture.

If the talib's element is fire and the maṭlūb's element is earth, the heat of the fire is tempered by the coldness of the earth. Two degrees of dryness remain, and the two cannot achieve harmony with one another.

If the talib's element is fire and the maṭlūb's element is air, the dryness of the fire is tempered by the moisture of the air. Two degrees of fire remain, and the two are in harmony with one another.

If the talib's element is fire and the maṭlūb's element is water, the heat of the fire is tempered by the coldness of the water; likewise the dryness of the fire is tempered by the moisture of the water, and the two are in harmony with one another.
If the talib's element is earth and the maṭlūb's element is fire, the coldness of the earth tempers the heat of the fire. Because two degrees of dryness remain, they can never achieve harmony.

If the talib's element is earth and the maṭlūb's element is air, the coldness of the earth is tempered by the heat of the air; likewise the dryness of the earth is tempered by the moisture of the air, and they achieve harmony.
If the talib's element is earth and the maṭlūb's element is water, the dryness of the earth is tempered by the moisture of the water.
Because two degrees of coldness remain, they can never achieve harmony.
If the talib's element is air and the maṭlūb's element is fire, the moisture of the air is tempered by the heat of the fire. Because two degrees of fire remain, they are in accord with one another.

[I 18] If the talib's element is air and the maṭlūb's element is earth, the heat of the air is tempered by the coldness of the earth; likewise the moisture of the air is tempered by the dryness of the earth, and they achieve harmony.
If the talib's element is air and the maṭlūb's is water, the heat of the air is tempered by the moisture of the water. Because two degrees of moisture remain, they are in accord with one another.

If the talib's element is water and the maṭlūb's element is fire, the coldness of the water tempers the heat of the fire; likewise the moisture of the water tempers the dryness of the fire, and they achieve harmony with one another.
If the talib's element is water and the maṭlūb's element is earth, the moisture of the water is tempered by the dryness of the earth.
Because two degrees of coldness remain, they cannot achieve harmony with one another.

If the talib's element is water and the maṭlūb's element is air, the coldness of the water is tempered by the heat of the air. Because two degrees of moisture remain, they achieve harmony with one another.

If the natures of the talib and the maṭlūb agree in heat or in moisture, they achieve harmony with one another. Fire with fire, earth with earth, air with air, water with water — these are always in harmony with one another.
The Friendship and Enmity of the Elements Toward One Another
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 18
Fire is a friend to Air and an enemy to Water. Earth is a friend to Water and an enemy to Air. Air is a friend to Fire and an enemy to Earth. Water is a friend to Earth and an enemy to Fire.
